text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Real Slovak GDP rose 5.1 percent year-on- year in the first quarter of this year.

- Local money market dealers attributed the Slovak crown uptrend over the past few days to high interbank rates offering a large interest rate differential with western countries and to the gradual strengthening of the Czech crown.
- ING Barings expects the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) will need to tap international sources to boost its foreign exchange reserves later this year.
- Official forecasts expect real GDP to grow by some 5.6 percent this year, inflation should not exceed 6.4 percent and the unemployment rate should be around 12.5 percent.
- Money market rates still trade at above 30 percent and traders do not expect any significant fall in the near future.
PRAVDA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said he was willing to start talks with President Michal Kovac, his bitter political enemy, on easing of political tensions in Slovakia.

- All major opposition parties on Wednesday refused to take part in a round table discussion with the ruling coalition, saying they would not hold talks with a government which includes Interior Minister Gustav Krajci accused by the opposition of thwarting the NATO and presidential referendums.
- Several Slovak commercial banks have increased interest rates on short-term primary deposits to about 20 percent due to an accute liquidity shortage on the money market.
SME - President Kovac on Wednesday officially appointed Zdenka Kramplova to the post of foreign minister.
- Kramplova said she would follow the government foreign policy programme and continue the policies of her predecessor Pavol Hamzik.
HOSPODARSEK NOVINY - The average monthly wage in Slovakia totalled 8,198 crowns in the first quarter of this year.

PRACA - The Constitutional Court has still to rule on the appeal by Frantisek Gaulider against his expulsion from parliament last autumn. The court said it would rule on the appeal by the end of this month.
- Gaulider said he would appeal to the international human right court in Strasbourg to change the ruling withdrawing his parliamentary mandate.
